module_name: Misinformation, Rumor Detection, and Trust & Safety
module_description: Module 19 treats false information as an analytics problem: diffusion of rumors vs corrections, stance detection toward claims, claim matching and fact-checking pipelines, bot-amplified false claims, and platform content moderation as a data source. Students learn to build a claim-verification pipeline (retrieve, cluster, match to fact-checks) and to measure correction effectiveness.
core_concepts: Rumor vs misinformation vs disinformation taxonomy
Rumor diffusion curves and correction spread
learning_outcomes: C3 Build a stance detection pipeline for a claim corpus
C5 Discuss limits of automatic veracity classification
methods_models: Stance classification (BERT-based), claim clustering and deduplication, temporal diffusion comparison (claim vs correction), credibility network features
evaluation_metrics: Accuracy/macro-F1 for stance and veracity, Agree/Disagree/No stance tri-class metrics, AUC-PR for rare claims, human spot-check of corrections
pitfalls_limitations: Ground truth ambiguity (fact-check scope), temporal leakage, correction measurement confounded by platform reach, dialect/code-mixing hurting stance models
tools_stack: transformers for stance, claim-cluster tools, fact-check API integrations (Google Fact Check API), returns
tools_access_cost: Fact-check APIs are free; annotation work is the real cost
lab_activities: Stance detection on an issue corpus, then compare diffusion of a claim vs its correction
datasets_apis: Indonesian hoax/fact-check datasets plus live claim corpora
assessment_methods: Lab notebook plus graph figures and a short interpretation; graded on correctness of metrics and defensibility of substantive claims
data_collection_workflow: Build the interaction graph from collected data -> deduplicate accounts and edges -> compute metrics -> cluster communities -> archive graph object and code
textbooks: Jurafsky & Martin, ch. on stance/NLP for social good
key_papers: 2024-2026 scoping reviews of generative AI and misinformation (e.g. Park 2026)
arXiv 2505.10266 characterizing AI-generated misinformation on X
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: generative AI scaled both the volume and the credibility of false claims; detection shifted towards provenance, watermarking and behavioral signals rather than pure text classifiers
industry_relevance: Used in disinformation/trust-and-safety teams, political-communication research units, community-management analytics, and influence-marketing measurement; network metrics are standard deliverables in crisis-mapping briefings.
localization_context: Practised on Indonesian case networks (election-issue discussion, anti-hoax communities, local brand mentions) where the platform mix and language mix differ from US/EU benchmark datasets.
ethics_regulation: Re-identification risk of pseudonymous accounts, doxxing risk when publishing ego-networks, and the ethical line between mapping influence and surveilling individuals; UU PDP applies to any data tied to identifiable accounts.
case_study_scenarios: Track a local hoax claim, its spread and the effect of fact-checks.
